_about: Saints outside the calendar whose date neither Wikidata, the Wikipedia infobox nor a review decision confirms. 'kept': true means the saint is still shown on that date; 'kept': false means it is left out (no Wikipedia article to describe it). 'removed' lists saints taken out by Scripts/saint_date_review.json, with the reason.

removed.name: The Eternal Father
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). Wikipedia: "God the Father is a title given to God in Christianity"; not a saint and not a liturgical feast in the calendar.

removed.name: The Circumcision of Our Lord
removed.reason: USCCB (https://www.usccb.org/prayer-and-worship/liturgical-year/christmas/christmas-january-1): 1 January is the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God, already on the calendar.

removed.name: The Baptism of Our Lord
removed.reason: Old fixed date; the Baptism of the Lord is movable and named from the liturgical day.

removed.name: Peter
removed.reason: Pre-1960 Chair of St. Peter at Rome; its only support was the infobox's "18 January: Confession of Saint Peter (Anglicanism, Lutheranism)". St. Peter is on the calendar on 22 February and 29 June.

removed.name: Holy Martyrs of Japan
removed.reason: The entry describes Paul Miki and companions, celebrated on 6 February (on the calendar); its link was to the Martyrs of Jasenovac.

removed.name: Abraham and Mary his Niece
removed.reason: Not settled: the infobox lists several dates, none 16 March and none marked Roman Catholic. Left out until checked against the Roman Martyrology.

removed.name: Simon
removed.reason: Simon of Trent: his death was used as a blood libel against the Jews of Trent, and "on 28 October 1965 ... archbishop of Trent Alessandro Maria Gottardi abolished the cult of Simon" (Wikipedia, Simon of Trent). He is not in the 2004 Martyrology's index of names.

removed.name: John
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). The pre-1969 English Roman Martyrology (https://www.ecatholic2000.com/roman-martyrology/05-may.shtml) has "At Rome, the feast of St. John before the Latin Gate" on 6 May. St. John is celebrated on 27 December.

removed.name: Avitus
removed.reason: The entry describes Avitus, abbot near Orléans, but linked the Roman emperor Avitus; no Wikipedia article for the abbot was found.

removed.name: The Commemoration of Saint Paul
removed.reason: Pre-1969 commemoration; St. Paul is celebrated with St. Peter on 29 June (on the calendar), and the 2004 Martyrology index lists him at 29 June.

removed.name: Most Precious Blood of Jesus
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). The pre-1969 English Roman Martyrology (https://www.ecatholic2000.com/roman-martyrology/07-jul.shtml) has "Feast of the Most Precious Blood of Our Lord Jesus Christ" on 1 July.

removed.name: Anacletus
removed.reason: The same pope as Cletus (both entries link the Wikipedia article Pope Anacletus); the 2004 Martyrology has one entry, "Cletus Pp, 26 apr., 1 (88)", and the app keeps him on 26 April. 13 July was the pre-1960 separate feast of Anacletus.

removed.name: Peter
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). The pre-1969 English Roman Martyrology (https://www.ecatholic2000.com/roman-martyrology/08-aug.shtml) has "At Rome, on Mount Esquiline, the dedication of the church of St. Peter in Chains" on 1 August. St. Peter is on the calendar on 22 February and 29 June.

removed.name: Joseph Chiwatenhwa
removed.reason: Not in the index of names of the 2004 Martyrologium Romanum (https://archive.org/details/MartRom2004), which lists the saints and blesseds whose cult is recognised. His Wikipedia article describes him as an "Early Christian convert in Canada".

removed.name: The Dedication of Saint Mary of the Snows
removed.reason: Duplicate of the calendar's Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major (5 August).

removed.name: Transfiguration of Our Lord
removed.reason: Duplicate of the calendar's Transfiguration of the Lord (6 August).

removed.name: Philomena
removed.reason: Not in the 2004 Martyrology's index of names; her Wikipedia article says she was "never formally canonized in the Catholic Church". Removed at Craig's decision (18 November 2026).

removed.name: The Dormition of Mary
removed.reason: Wikipedia (Dormition of the Mother of God): a Great Feast of the Eastern Orthodox, Oriental Orthodox and Eastern Catholic Churches; "In Western Churches the corresponding feast is known as the Assumption of Mary", which the calendar celebrates on 15 August.

removed.name: Liberatus
removed.reason: The entry describes Liberatus, abbot, martyred with six companions under Huneric (it linked the historian Liberatus of Carthage). The Vatican's martyr list (https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_academies/cult-martyrum/martiri/009.html) has them on 2 July, not 17 August: "A Cartagine, ricordo dei SS. martiri Liberato, abate, Bonifacio, diacono...". Left out: no Wikipedia article to describe them.

removed.name: The Immaculate Heart of Mary
removed.reason: Former fixed date; now the Saturday after the Sacred Heart, named from the liturgical day. 22 August is the Queenship (on the calendar).

removed.name: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist
removed.reason: Duplicate of the calendar's Passion of Saint John the Baptist (29 August).

removed.name: Maximin Giraud
removed.reason: Not in the index of names of the 2004 Martyrologium Romanum (https://archive.org/details/MartRom2004), which lists the saints and blesseds whose cult is recognised.

removed.name: Thecla
removed.reason: Thecla of Iconium is not in the 2004 Martyrology (its only Thecla is the abbess of Kitzingen, 15 October). Removed at Craig's decision (19 November 2026), as Philomena was.

removed.name: Our Lady of Ransom
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). The pre-1969 English Roman Martyrology (https://www.ecatholic2000.com/roman-martyrology/09-sep.shtml) has "The feast of our Lady of Ransom" on 24 September: a feast of the old calendar.

removed.name: Jeanne Leber
removed.reason: Not in the index of names of the 2004 Martyrologium Romanum (https://archive.org/details/MartRom2004), which lists the saints and blesseds whose cult is recognised.

removed.name: The Feast of the Holy Redeemer
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). Wikipedia (Feast of the Most Holy Redeemer): "found only in the special calendar of some dioceses and religious orders", on the third Sunday of July or 23 October.

removed.name: The Feast of the Holy Relics
removed.reason: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). Wikipedia (Relic): "In the Extraordinary Form of the Catholic Church, the Feast of the Holy Relics is celebrated on 5 November": the pre-1969 calendar, not the current one.

removed.name: Peter
removed.reason: Duplicate of the calendar's Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul (18 November).

removed.name: Catherine Labouré
removed.reason: Duplicate: she is placed on 31 December, her Roman Martyrology date.

removed.name: Melanie Calvat
removed.reason: Not in the index of names of the 2004 Martyrologium Romanum (https://archive.org/details/MartRom2004), which lists the saints and blesseds whose cult is recognised.

removed.name: The Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ
removed.reason: Duplicate of the Nativity of the Lord (on the calendar).
